title: Rectangular block
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. Begin with the first loop, drawing the first line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.1023, 0.0), then the second line from (0.1023, 0.0) to (0.1023, 0.75), followed by the third line from (0.1023, 0.75) to (0.0, 0.75), and finally the fourth line from (0.0, 0.75) back to the origin. After completing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using Euler angles of zero and translating it using a vector of zero. Extrude the sketch 0.0293 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. This results in a rectangular block with a length of 0.1023 meters, a width of 0.75 meters, and a height of 0.0293 meters. This completes the construction of the first expert part, forming the base of the rectangular block.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.box(0.1023, 0.75, 0.0293, centered=(False, False, False))

# The box function creates a box with the given dimensions
# The centered parameter is set to False to ensure the box starts from the origin (0, 0, 0)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · best of 8
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1023, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1023, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a rectangular bar
r = r.extrude(0.0293)
